children: There’s no direct proof, but it’s a plausible theory. The sun is often cast as a symbol of Christ, and Christian festivals tend to fall on at important points of the solar cycle: Christmas on the Winter Solstice and Easter on the Vernal Equinox.
Jesus also bears more than a slight resemblance to the Roman god
Sol Invictus
(“Unconquered Sun”), whose birth seems to have been celebrated on December 25.
Some scholars have theorized
that the date of Christmas Day was chosen to coincide with this, but the theory does not currently hold much sway.

Wikimedia Commons.
